messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a regression after the last kernel_selector tweak. p99 latency for short-stream requests jumped ~2.3x during peak. Flamegraph points at queue handoff and KV thrash. link: https://perf.internal/runs/1761213141 :eyes:

jon: Ugh. Is this only on small sequence workloads or across the board? Any baseline numbers?

maya: Mostly small-seq (<64) streaming and prefill-heavy mixes. Quick numbers from canary vs prod:
- canary (old selector): p50 12ms, p95 38ms, p99 79ms
- prod (new selector): p50 13ms, p95 62ms, p99 184ms
(Metrics from 10k samples window)

liam: Sounds like prefill ops are being batched with decode and starving decode or vice-versa. Did kernel_selector change affinity to fused kernels? Those can increase kernel latency for small batches.

sasha: Confirmed. The selector now prefers kernel X when estimated batch_size>=8, but batch formation is mixing prefill requests that pad batches to hit that heuristics. Result: more big-kernel invocations that hurt short-paths. I pulled a trace:
```
trace_id: 0x7fa1
stage: prefill -> batching -> kernelX (heavy) -> kv_evict -> decode starve
avg_kv_evictions/sec: 12
```

dave: Two immediate mitigations we can flip:
1) Enforce phase-aware queue separation: prefill queue vs decode queue + different batching thresholds.
2) Add token_budget ceilings so prefill can't grow batch shapes past N tokens that trigger kernel X.

jon: Both sound good. Any config sketch?

dave: Here's a quick example we can try in canary:
```json
{
  "queues": {
    "prefill": {"scheduler": "fifo", "batch_min": 2, "batch_max_tokens": 800, "token_budget": 2000},
    "decode":  {"scheduler": "latency_pref", "batch_min": 1, "batch_max_tokens": 256,  "token_budget": 512}
  },
  "kernel_selector": {"prefer_fused_threshold_tokens": 1024}
}
```
Note: batch_max_tokens is per-batch token budget, token_budget is per-queue circulation cap.

maya: I'll push that to the canary routing layer and run a 6-hour soak against the streaming workload.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: ✅ started canary job redwood/queue-split/1761213141 at 2024-08-11T14:32:00Z

jon: Also want to capture KV cache hit rates before/after. If prefill batches are too large they evict important KV entries.

sasha: Attached quick profiling snippet for KV pressure:
```
KV cache size: 12M entries
Evictions/sec: was 1.2 -> peaked to 13.4 on prod
Avg KV access latency: 0.9ms -> 4.1ms
Cache hit ratio: 0.86 -> 0.57
```

maya: Canary run finished. Short summary: separate queues + token ceilings reduced p99 for streaming short-seq by ~45%. KV evictions down from 13.4/s to 2.1/s. Full numbers:
- before: p99 184ms, KV evict 13.4/s, hit 0.57
- after: p99 102ms,  KV evict 2.1/s, hit 0.82

liam: Nice. Any regressions for large-batch throughput?

maya: Throughput for bulk-prefill jobs dropped ~3% peak (expected) but overall tail improved. We're within SLA.

jon: Can we make token_budget adaptive? Maybe bump prefill token_budget when GPU utilization <70% so we don't regress throughput during slack.

dave: Good idea. We can implement a simple proportional controller:
```
if gpu_util < 0.7: prefill.token_budget = min(max_budget, prefill.token_budget * 1.2)
else: prefill.token_budget = max(min_budget, prefill.token_budget * 0.85)
```
We should guard with cooldown windows.

sasha: Also want to add a metric: batch_shape_histogram per queue (tokens x seq_len) so kernel_selector can make informed decisions without one-size thresholds.

jon: Agreed. Please open a follow-up ticket and add to the perf dashboard.

maya: Filed PERF-1289 with experiment artifacts + bench scripts: https://issues.internal/PERF-1289 :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy-canary: ✅ finished canary job redwood/queue-split/1761213141 (status: succeeded)

liam: Next steps:
- roll queue split to more clusters behind a staged rollout
- implement adaptive token_budget controller
- add batch_shape histogram to metrics
- refine kernel_selector to consult per-queue histograms

jon: I'll own the rollout plan with SRE. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — will drop the raw traces and flamegraphs in PERF-1289.

sasha: Great outcome. Worth writing a short postmortem note for release notes so customers see improved tail.

maya: Agree. I'll draft one and ping marketing for a short blurb. :writing_hand:
